title: Character Lifecycle
summary: Players join once; CHARACTERS are repeatedly created and destroyed on each spawn/respawn. CharacterAdded/CharacterRemoving + respawns resetting state is the #1 source of 'it broke after I died' bugs.

explanation.whatItIs: Player = the persistent account object. Character = a disposable body, rebuilt every spawn. Anything parented to or cached on the character dies with it.
explanation.whyItExists: Death needs a clean slate: fresh body, fresh position, fresh health.
whenToUse: CharacterAdded for per-life setup (tools, modifiers, GUI hooks)
Store persistent data on the PLAYER (or server tables), never the Character
Re-apply systems on every respawn — cached references go stale
Humanoid.Died for death handling; wait for the new Character after
whenNotToUse: Caching character parts at join time — they'll be replaced
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Player joins ────────────────────────► (persists)
  Character #1 ── dies ── X
  Character #2 ── falls  ── X        ← new object each time
  Character #3 ── alive

Rule: attach lasting state to the PLAYER,
      attach life-scoped state to the CHARACTER (reapplied per spawn).
```
tips: player.Character can be nil between spawns — always guard
Server tables keyed by Player are the robust 'session data' home
commonMistakes: Connections to a character's Humanoid never reconnected after respawn
Speed boosts applied once at join, lost at first death
Assuming player.Character exists in PlayerAdded (it may not yet)

examples.title: Per-life setup that survives respawns
examples.code:
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    -- Persistent/session stuff here:
    setupLeaderstats(player)

    -- Per-life stuff goes in CharacterAdded:
    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(character)
        local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
        humanoid.WalkSpeed = 16 * getSpeedMultiplier(player)

        humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
            onPlayerDeath(player)
        end)
    end)
end)
